Stanford Bachata & Zouk Club: Fall Transition & Leadership Roster

Hey everyone! As many of you know, this is going to be my last quarter at Stanford. I’ve enjoyed teaching and organizing Bachata and Zouk classes over the years and I hope that they will continue after I graduate for many years to come. Outside of classes and conferences and research, this club has been a very fulfilling experience, not just for dance, but because of all the people I had a chance to meet and  get to know.
As we prep for the upcoming academic year, we are transitioning leadership and setting up our official Stanford ASSU/OSE club roster for studio space, funding, and campus events.
If you are an enrolled Stanford student (Undergrad, Grad, or Postdoc):
Please take 60 seconds to fill out this quick form so we can confirm our official student base and identify our next leadership board:

(Note: Community members and alumni are always welcome at our socials and open practices, but only matriculated Stanford students can serve as official ASSU officers and secure university space/grants)

If you love these dances and want real leadership/management experience running socials, bringing in guest instructors, and managing club funding, check out the officer section in the form. Let’s keep Zouk and Bachata thriving on campus!
Stanford Undergraduate (Frosh / Soph / Junior / Senior / Co-term)
Other partner dances (Salsa, Tango, West Coast Swing, etc.)
Complete beginner (< 3 months; excited to learn!)
Beginner / Intermediate (3 - 12 months; taken a few classes/socials)
Intermediate / Advanced (12+ months; social dance regularly)

The club needs an official student leadership team to secure spaces, manage ASSU funding, and run weekly classes/socials. Time commitment is a few hours at the beginning of each quarter + light weekly communications (emails/whatsapp). Would you be interested in taking a role?
Maybe / Open to a small or supportive role
No, just want to participate as a dancer
Vision, strategy, event planning, and university administrative liaison
ASSU grant writing, budget allocation, instructor payments, and banking
WhatsApp/social media, room reservations, newsletter, and event marketing
Sound setup, social logistics, DJ curation, beginner check-ins, instructor outreach & coordination
Tell us briefly why you’d like to get involved or what you’d like to see the club do this year:
Notes: Stanford Tango Lessons for Bachata/Zouk
1) Email is their most effective communications channel. Also use IG and WhatsApp, but emails at the start of the week announcing upcoming classes are most effective.

2) Club fairs (separate grad and undergrad ones at the start of each academic year) are the biggest source of new members. Need to register and plan booth staffing and presence (banners? info sheets? demos?)
Cross promotion with other dance groups including Dancebreak (and also verbal announcements at the event)
Flyers at Richard Powers dance classes + in-class announcement

4) Leadership recruiting: Direct conversations with potential leaders based on personality and active participation in the club. Time commitment is limited: a few hours at the start of each quarter to reserve rooms, organize teachers. Weekly email post (plus IG and WhatsApp as needed). Need to cultivate next generation of leaders on an ongoing basis (i.e. every year).

Leila shared insights on running a successful student dance club, specifically to help with the transition of leadership for the Bachata and Zouk club at Stanford. Leila shared her experience with the Tango Club, detailing how they recruited members through club fairs, Instagram, and Richard Powers' dance classes. She explained the challenges of space reservation, budgeting, and university policies regarding community participation and fundraising. Leila described the informal leadership structure of the Tango Club, emphasizing that members joined out of passion for the dance rather than for resume-building. She also discussed the time commitment for leadership, which was mostly upfront work at the start of each quarter. The conversation covered communication methods, such as email and WhatsApp, and the importance of finding committed individuals to ensure the club's continuity.
the Bachata/Zouk club has applied for the annual ASSU grant and confirm the status of the financial officer.
Forward the standing reservation form request for Roble Gym
Confirm whether B/Z has signed up for Club Fair and has booth staffing plans

Leila discussed her experience with the tango club, explaining that she initially attended lessons as a freshman but found the diverse age groups uncomfortable. She returned later in her freshman year and discovered she enjoyed tango. Leila eventually joined the club's leadership as vice president in her sophomore year after the graduating seniors asked for help. Most effective recruitment channel for leadership team:
Direct personal appeals to join the leadership team by current leaders
as well as volunteers asking to do more.

Dan and Leila discussed the leadership transition of a student dance club, particularly focusing on the Tango Club at Stanford. Leila explained that her motivation to take on leadership came from wanting to help after being inspired by the tango.
Leila explained that while dance clubs face challenges in recruiting students due to time constraints, they naturally attract interest through club fairs and social media channels. She noted that
email is the most effective communication channel

, though the club also uses Instagram and the cards system run by the Associated Students. Leila mentioned that students often sign up for their mailing list and follow their Instagram without specific advertising to them.

Leila explained that student recruitment for their tango club primarily happens through ASSU announcements and club fairs at the beginning of the year, with the undergrad club fair scheduled for September 30th to October 2nd and the grad club fair on September 18th. She mentioned that Richard Powers' dance classes, which attract 60-70 students each, are also effective recruitment channels, with opportunities to place flyers and make announcements during class. When asked about relevance for other dance styles like Bachata, Leila indicated that Bachata would likely be appropriate since it's similar to what Powers teaches in Social Dance 1.

Leila discussed the promotion of tango classes at Stanford Ballroom, mentioning that they currently teach basic bachata moves and have offered classes at Dance Break. She highlighted the success of their performances at the Viennese Ball, which helped showcase the potential of tango to a wider audience. Leila noted that while they have a core group of dedicated dancers, there is no specific incentive for students to continue beyond basic lessons, making retention a challenge.

Leila explained the process for reserving university spaces for dance activities, including options like EBGR studios, Havana Room, Kennedy grad room, Robley studios through the Department of Theater and Performance Studies, and EPC. She noted specific rules and quotas for different spaces, such as the two-week advance reservation limit at EPC and the twice-a-quarter limit at the Havana room. Leila also mentioned that Koret is the only space where payment is required.

Leila explained that the tango club receives its annual grant from ASSU but learned two years ago that accepting outside donations directly from community members must go through the university. She mentioned that two dance groups were previously penalized for allowing non-Stanford students to pay for lessons, leading to stricter enforcement of university policies.

discussed the financial aspects, including the need for a financial officer to apply for grants and the costs of paying instructors, with recent sessions costing around $2,000 total. Leila outlined the leadership structure and recruitment process, noting that the leadership team's time commitment varies but typically involves 3 hours of work at the beginning of each quarter followed by attending regular lessons. She also mentioned upcoming workshops with an Italian instructor and the implementation of an RSVP system for these events.
